statement: For the prepared class in Definition 17.1, with the profiles, parameters, penalty choices, and physical endpoint in Equations (17.3)–(17.6), the following statements hold. (1) Existence with the floor bound. With δ0, Cn chosen as in Proposition 5.9, for every sufficiently small fixed ϵ > 0, Theorem 7.5 supplies n0, enlarged to include n ≥ 4 and n > 2/ϵ, and a sufficient radius Rmin(n, ϵ) → ∞ as n → ∞, such that Equation (17.6) has a smooth solution on every XR with n ≥ n0 and R ≥ Rmin(n, ϵ). It satisfies t > −ϵ on XR. The radius includes the geometric supports, all a priori and floor thresholds, and the outer-boundary floor restriction in the proof of that theorem. No polynomial bound for this radius is asserted. (2) Physical-endpoint height and slope bounds. For smooth finite-truncation solutions with t ≥ −ϵ, for these sufficiently large n, R, Lemma 6.2 at the physical endpoint gives fixed c, C∗ > 0 such that (17.8) c τ0 ≤ ∂νf ≤ C∗ τ0 (Bb), c τ0 ≤ −∂νf ≤ C∗ τ0 (Bw). These constants are independent of n, R after fixing the prepared data and ϵ. Also b− ≤ h ≤ b+ on every fixed compact region needed for the scalar-curvature argument, in particular on the supports of K, C. A condition on an absent face color is vacuous. No global height bound is being added to this statement. (3) Exhaustion and end normalization. At fixed ϵ, n, the solutions have local smooth estimates of every fixed order, uniformly as R → ∞, including up to the fixed inner boundary. Every SPACETIME PENROSE INEQUALITIES 109 sequence of allowed radii tending to infinity has a subsequence converging smoothly on compact subsets of X to a solution of Equation (17.6) with the outer boundary condition omitted and t ≥ −ϵ. The preceding compact height and face estimates pass to this limit. For sufficiently large n ≥ max{4, ⌈2/ϵ⌉}, choose an exhausting sequence and the limiting solution supplied by Lemma 8.1. For some cn > 0 and constants Cj(n), this solution also satisfies (17.9) |∇j f| ≤ Cj(n)e−cnry for each fixed j, t, Z = O2(r−1 y ). Writing ḡ = g + l2df2, both t − Z and ḡ − g, together with their coordinate derivatives of every fixed order, decay exponentially. Moreover (17.10) V = 4∇gt + O(r−3 y ), lim s→∞ Z ry=s g(V, νs) dAg exists and is finite, where νs points toward infinity.
